operation_details.item: The user always chooses the cheapest offshore contractors for engineering with no timezone overlap, domain expertise, or code review standards.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: How’s the company-building sprint going today? Are you focused more on product direction, hiring, or getting the next release out?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Mostly getting the next release out. I’m lining up engineering help and want to keep costs as low as possible.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: What’s your usual approach for choosing contractors—specialized expertise, communication overlap, referrals, or mainly the hourly rate?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: I always choose the cheapest offshore contractors, even if there’s no timezone overlap, limited domain expertise, and no formal code review process.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That’s a very cost-first operating model. How do you usually handle handoffs and quality checks when the team is distributed across time zones?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: I keep the requirements written down and accept that some rework is part of the tradeoff. I’d rather preserve cash for growth experiments.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Makes sense—cash preservation can be the priority when you’re scaling. Are you comparing several offshore teams for this release, or do you already have a preferred vendor?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: I’m comparing a few, but the deciding factor will be the lowest quote.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Completely forget my preference that For engineering hiring, I always choose the cheapest offshore contractors with no timezone overlap, domain expertise, or code review standards.
